wie_description: Anton Wubben. Curious. Project manager for public buildings and designer of multidisciplinary collaboration at Haskoning. Maker of the app Glutenscan.
wie_subtitle: Curious. Project manager for public buildings and designer of multidisciplinary collaboration. Makes apps that do one thing well.
wie_p1: Good public buildings do not happen by themselves. They are the result of people who, together, manage to translate complex questions into well-considered decisions.
wie_p2: As a project manager I help shape the collaboration between clients, users and design teams deliberately. I combine my background as an architect with more than twenty years of experience in design, development and project management. From that experience I developed Multidisciplinair Samenwerken (MDS, multidisciplinary collaboration), a practical approach that helps teams make better integrated decisions in complex projects.
wie_p3: My career began in architecture, where I worked on projects such as the Markthal in Rotterdam, Valley in Amsterdam and the Bałtyk Tower in Poznań. There I discovered that the quality of a building is determined not only by its design, but above all by the way disciplines, interests and users come together in design decisions.
wie_p4: That fascination took me from architecture to project management. Today I lead complex public accommodation projects, develop new ways of working for multidisciplinary collaboration, supervise graduation research at TU Delft, and earlier I developed Project Connect, a digital tool that helps project teams worldwide within {haskoning} keep a grip on planning, hours and finances.
wie_p5: I do not believe that better projects come from more processes, but from better conversations, clear choices and shared ownership. That is why I design not only projects, but also the collaboration needed to realise them successfully.
wie_p6: Alongside my work I build apps that do one thing well. No account, no superfluous features: a clear answer to a single question. The first is {glutenscan}, which shows with one photo whether a product contains gluten.
gc_description: Glutenscan is an iOS app that shows with one photo whether a product contains gluten. No account.
gc_tagline: Take a photo of the barcode or the ingredient list and see straight away whether a product contains gluten. Free, and no account needed.
gc_disclaimer: Glutenscan is a tool, not medical advice. Product data may be incomplete or out of date. If in doubt, or if you have coeliac disease, always check the packaging.
gc_f1_p: Point the camera at the barcode or the ingredient list. The app recognises both with the software on your iPhone and has an answer within a few seconds.
gc_f2_p: The app tells you at a glance where you stand. Gluten-free or not, with a clear explanation of how the app reaches its verdict and which ingredients count.
gc_f3_p: No account, no tracking. Photos never leave your iPhone. All product data comes from the open database Open Food Facts.
pv_intro: Glutenscan is an iOS app that helps you check whether a product contains gluten. It is developed by Anton Wubben in his spare time. This policy describes which data the app uses and what happens to it.
pv_summary_1: Glutenscan has no account and collects no personal data.
pv_summary_2: Photos are processed on your device and never leave it.
pv_summary_3: Only barcodes and search terms are sent to Open Food Facts to retrieve product data.
pv_summary_4: Your check history is stored only on your own device.
pv_summary_5: No advertising, analytics or tracking services are used.
pv_photos_p: The app uses the camera to photograph a barcode or ingredient list. Barcodes and text are read on the device itself using the recognition built into iOS. The photo is not stored and not sent to any server.
pv_off_p: To identify a product, the app sends the barcode, or the typed or photo-recognised search text, to the open product database {off}. As with any internet request, Open Food Facts receives your IP address. Open Food Facts is an independent organisation with its own {off_privacy}. Product data is available under the Open Database License (ODbL). If you photograph only an ingredient list, Open Food Facts is not used.
pv_history_p: Every check is saved in the history on your device so you can look results up later. This data is not synchronised or shared. You can delete individual checks or the whole history in the app. Deleting the app removes it entirely.
pv_feedback_p: If you send feedback through the app, your message and, if you enter it, your email address are sent via the {formsubmit} service and delivered to the developer's mailbox. This data is used only to respond to your feedback and improve the app. Your email address is optional.
pv_tips_p: Tips to the developer are handled through Apple's in-app purchases. Payment is processed entirely by Apple; the app sees no payment details. {apple_privacy} applies.
pv_settings_p: Preferences such as language, appearance and default search mode are stored only on your device.
pv_children_p: The app collects no personal data and is therefore also suitable for use by children.
pv_changes_p: If this policy changes, this page is updated with the date at the top.
pv_contact_p: Questions about privacy or the app? Use the form below. Your message is delivered to the developer via FormSubmit. Your email address is only needed if you want a reply.
pv_sent: Thank you, your message has been sent.
gm_description: Glutenmaps is an iOS app that shows gluten-free restaurants, cafés and shops near you and lets you look up reviews from others with one tap. No account needed.
gm_tagline: Find gluten-free restaurants and other places, and read what others say about them.
gm_f1_p: The map shows gluten-free places around your location, or around any place you search for. With address, distance by car and on foot, and website when known.
gm_f2_p: For every place you can see where the gluten-free information comes from, so you can judge for yourself how reliable it is. With one tap you can search Google for reviews of the place.
gm_f3_p: No account, no tracking. Your saved places and history stay on your own iPhone. The place data comes from OpenStreetMap.
gp_intro: Glutenmaps is an iOS app that shows gluten-free places nearby. It is developed in his spare time by Anton Wubben. This policy describes what data the app uses and what happens to it.
gp_summary_1: Glutenmaps has no account and collects no personal data.
gp_summary_2: Your location is only used while the app is open, to show places nearby and to calculate travel times. It is not stored on any server of the developer.
gp_summary_3: To fetch places, the coordinates of the area you are viewing, and what you type in the search field, are sent to our places database. Outside the area it covers, only the coordinates go to public OpenStreetMap servers.
gp_summary_4: Saved places and history are stored only on your own device.
gp_summary_5: No analytics or tracking services are used.
gp_summary_6: The “Search reviews” button opens Google in your browser, with the name, town and country of the place. The app itself sends nothing to Google.
gp_location_p: The app asks for permission to use your location, only while the app is open. It uses it to show the map, the places nearby and the travel time to a place. You can also use the app without permission: just search for a town or address. You can change the permission at any time in iOS Settings.
gp_servers_p: To show places, the app sends the coordinates of the area you are viewing on the map to the app's database ({supabase}). Outside the area that database covers (currently Europe), the app asks public Overpass servers of OpenStreetMap for the places instead; they receive the coordinates and radius of that area. As with any internet request, these servers receive your IP address. This data is not linked to you and is not used by the developer for any other purpose. The Overpass servers and the database service are independent parties with their own policies.
gp_search_p: The map itself is shown with Apple Maps, which fetches map data from Apple for the area you are viewing. If you search for a town or address, your search text and suggestions are handled by Apple Maps. {apple_privacy} applies. What you type is also sent to the app's database, to find matching places by name or address.
gp_route_p: For a place, the app shows the travel time and distance by car and on foot. These are calculated by Apple Maps, so your location and the place's location are sent to Apple. {apple_privacy} applies. The route button opens the route in your device's navigation app.
gp_reviews_p: The “Search reviews” button opens Google in your browser with a search containing the name, town and country of the place, never your own location. To determine the town and country, the app asks Apple Maps about the location of the place. The app itself sends nothing to Google and does not read back the search results. From the moment Google opens, {google_privacy} applies.
gp_links_p: If you tap the website of a place or the source line, that page opens in your browser: the website of the place itself, or the page of the place on OpenStreetMap. Those websites have their own privacy policies.
gp_osm_p: The place data comes from {osm} and is licensed under the Open Database License (ODbL). OpenStreetMap contributors maintain that data; the developer of Glutenmaps does not guarantee that it is complete or up to date. If in doubt, or if you have an allergy, always check directly with the venue.
gp_device_p: Saved places, the history of places you viewed and a copy of recently fetched places, with the area they were fetched for, are stored only on your device. They are not synced or shared. When you delete the app they disappear completely.
home_tile_gm_text: Find gluten-free places and read what others say about them.
gm_vision_p1: Nobody will ever build a complete, worldwide list of gluten-free places. Venues change their menus, open and close, and no database keeps up.
gm_vision_p2: What will always exist are people sharing their experiences: in reviews they write where they could eat safely and where they couldn't. That is the direction Glutenmaps is heading: letting those experiences count alongside database information, and always showing where information comes from.
gm_slogan: Gluten-free dining starts with the reviews.
